panels.visual: Spartans carrying huge heavy iron bars as money, a wagon creaking under a pile of iron bars for a single purchase, a rich man sweating; Lycurgus (stern, dignified, from the sheet) overseeing with arms folded
panels.caption: Lycurgus is said to have given Sparta its laws, with money made of heavy iron bars so that nobody could get rich.

panels.visual: A split panel: left, a furious rich young man striking Lycurgus with a stick, Lycurgus clutching a hand over his eye (no blood); right, Lycurgus kindly leading the young man into his house, the young man bowing
panels.caption: A young man knocked out Lycurgus's eye. Lycurgus took him in, and he became his most loyal follower.

panels.visual: A crowd of Spartans raising their hands to swear an oath, and Lycurgus (one eye covered with a patch) walking away alone up a road toward Delphi at sunset, never looking back
panels.caption: He made the Spartans swear to keep his laws until he came back. He went to Delphi and never returned.

panels.visual: A different man, the Athenian Lycurgus (a statesman in 330 BC), supervising workers laying stone seats in the Theatre of Dionysus, and scribes copying scrolls of plays at a table; a big 'TWO MEN' sign with two different faces
panels.caption: Athens had its own Lycurgus, a real one, about 330 BC. He rebuilt the theatre in stone and had official copies made of the plays. Don't mix them up.
